findings.heading: Carregar pacotes / Load packages
findings.proposition: The English sends the reader to the R basics chapter (basics.qmd) for more on R packages; the Portuguese link target is #heatmaps, which is this chapter's own anchor (line 6 of the .pt.qmd), so it claims the R basics material is on this page.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader who follows the link stays on the heat plots page and never reaches the R basics chapter, so the pointer to package background is lost.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame dos casos / Make cases data frame
findings.proposition: The Portuguese prose says the data frame is called `idades_de_caso`; the chunk beside it creates `case_ages`, and every later chunk uses `case_ages`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader looks for an object named idades_de_caso that never exists, and cannot match the named data frame to the code they are told to run.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame de infectantes / Make infectors data frame
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first 50 rows of the `infectors` data frame are displayed below; the display chunk beside it calls DT::datatable(case_ages, ...), so it shows `case_ages`, not `infectors`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sees the cases table again instead of the single-column infectors table, so cannot verify that select(infector) + drop_na() produced one column of infector IDs.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame de infectantes / Make infectors data frame
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first 50 rows of the joined infector records (with age added) are displayed below; the display chunk beside it shows `case_ages` instead of `infector_ages`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot see that the join added the infector's age column, which is the whole point of the step being explained.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame de infectantes / Make infectors data frame
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first rows of the combined case-and-infector-age data frame are displayed below; the display chunk beside it shows `case_ages` instead of `ages_complete`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader never sees the combined data frame holding both case age and infector age, so cannot confirm the second join or the drop_na() step worked.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame de infectantes / Make infectors data frame
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first rows of the long-format counts table are displayed below; the display chunk beside it shows `case_ages` instead of `long_counts`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot see the long-format table that data.frame(table(...)) produces, which is the format the ggplot step depends on.

findings.heading: Criar um data frame de infectantes / Make infectors data frame
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first 50 rows of the proportions table are displayed below; the display chunk beside it shows `case_ages` instead of `long_prop`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader cannot see that prop.table() replaced counts with proportions, which is the value later mapped to fill in the heat plot.

findings.heading: Preparação / Data preparation (Reporting metrics over time)
findings.proposition: The prose states that the first 30 rows of the imported daily malaria facility dataset are shown below; the display chunk beside it calls DT::datatable(head(linelist, 30), ...), so it shows the Ebola case linelist instead of `facility_count_data`.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is shown the Ebola linelist and takes it for the malaria facility data, so does not learn the columns (location_name, data_date, District, malaria_tot) that the rest of the section manipulates.

findings.heading: Agregar e resumir / Aggregate and summarize
findings.proposition: The prose says the dataset is expanded to include every possible combination of the columns week and location_name; the chunk beside it calls tidyr::expand(week) with only one column, where the English chunk calls tidyr::expand(location_name, week).
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who runs the Portuguese code gets a one-column table of weeks, so the following right_join() does not fill in the missing facility-weeks, and the heat plot has no grey NA tiles the later text describes.

findings.heading: Agregar e resumir / Aggregate and summarize
findings.proposition: The English states the number of rows in expanded_weeks via inline R code (`r nrow(expanded_weeks)`); the Portuguese sentence drops the count entirely.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is not told how many facility-week combinations the expansion produced, so has no number to compare against the row count before and after the join.

findings.heading: Agregar e resumir / Aggregate and summarize
findings.proposition: The English states the row count of agg_weeks before the join via working inline R code (`r nrow(agg_weeks)`); the Portuguese drops the leading r, so the sentence renders the literal text nrow(agg_weeks) and states no number.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sees no before-join row count, so cannot check that the right_join() with expanded_weeks actually added rows.

findings.heading: Eixo y ordenado / Ordered y-axis
findings.proposition: The prose says to look at the data frame below, meaning `facility_order`; the display chunk beside it shows `case_ages` instead.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sees the transmission-matrix case table instead of the facilities ranked by total reporting days, so cannot see the ordering that sets the factor levels of the y-axis.

findings.heading: Eixo y ordenado / Ordered y-axis
findings.proposition: The prose introduces the code that uses facility_order$location_name to set the factor levels of location_name; the Portuguese chunk carries echo=F, so that code is not displayed, where the English chunk displays it.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is told to use a column to set the factor order but is shown no code, so never sees the fct_relevel() call that performs the step.
